packet.headline_seed: A deadly fungus that can infect cats and people is spreading
packet.description_seed: It’s just a matter of time before Sporothrix brasiliensis reaches the U.S. a CDC expert says.

what: A deadly fungus that can infect cats and people is spreading

clean_source_blocks.text: It’s just a matter of time before Sporothrix brasiliensis reaches the U.S. a CDC expert says.

WASHINGTON — Microbiologists are used to looking at gross pictures and hearing scary statistics. So when a moderator of a session on emerging fungal infections at the ASM Microbe meeting uttered the words “somewhat terrifying,” it caught my attention. He was referring to a sexually transmitted skin infection that is becoming increasingly drug resistant. But what came next was even more horrifying to me. Medical mycologist Shawn Lockhart stepped to the podium and began describing a fungal disease that attacks cats, causing oozing skin ulcers and worse, and spreads to humans. It isn’t yet in the United States … that officials know of. But the disease, caused by Sporothrix brasiliensis, has sickened and killed thousands of cats and infected more than 11,000 people and at least 200 dogs in South America since its emergence in Brazil in the 1990s. ---

original_article.research:
[Lähde: Science News]
WASHINGTON — Microbiologists are used to looking at gross pictures and hearing scary statistics. So when a moderator of a session on emerging fungal infections at the ASM Microbe meeting uttered the words “somewhat terrifying,” it caught my attention. He was referring to a sexually transmitted skin infection that is becoming increasingly drug resistant. But what came next was even more horrifying to me.

Medical mycologist Shawn Lockhart stepped to the podium and began describing a fungal disease that attacks cats, causing oozing skin ulcers and worse, and spreads to humans. It isn’t yet in the United States … that officials know of. But the disease, caused by Sporothrix brasiliensis, has sickened and killed thousands of cats and infected more than 11,000 people and at least 200 dogs in South America since its emergence in Brazil in the 1990s.

---

[Lähde: Hawaii News Now]
FAYETTEVILLE, Ark. (KFSM) - As summer approaches, vets are warning pet owners about “bobcat fever,” a deadly tick-borne disease that can infect domestic cats.

Originally hosted by bobcats, the disease can now affect domestic cats.

“Most folks that we diagnose it in are going to be your domestic cats, because those are the ones we’re bringing to the vet clinic,” Dr. Carley Allen of All Cats Clinic said.

Allen said once infected, the disease can progress quickly.

“Even just a few hours with that tick on them can transmit that to them,” Allen said.

While not every animal shows symptoms, there are signs to look out for.

“They’re just not feeling well, not feeling themselves, they don’t want to eat,” Allen said. “A lot of times they run a really high fever, and then as the disease progresses, we oftentimes will see that they’ll start getting icteric or yellowing of the skin.”

Allen said treatment often includes several medications.

“Appetite stimulants, anti-nausea meds, antiprotozoals and antibacterials to try to get them through that, get their immune system going,” Allen said.

But she said the best defense is prevention, through flea and tick medications that kill ticks quickly.

“Bravecto, Revolution Plus, any of those flea and tick treatments should keep the cat from getting infected,” Allen said.

With about a 60% survival rate, Allen said early detection can make all the difference.

Most importantly, she urged pet owners not to wait if their cat seems sick.

“If you’re noticing any sort of concerning clinical signs of your kitty not feeling well, getting them to a vet ASAP to get them checked out,” Allen said.

Copyright 2026 KFSM via CNN Newsource. All rights reserved.

---

[Lähde: KAIT]
JONESBORO, Ark. (KAIT) - A disease spread by ticks poses a deadly threat to cats, and experts say this season is one of the worst they have seen.

The Lone Star tick is spreading a disease called bobcat fever, and it has already killed several cats in the area in just the last few weeks.

The Lone Star tick can be spotted by the small white dot on its back.

Lisa Trevathan, community outreach coordinator for the NEA Humane Society, said the disease is spreading rapidly this year.

“Ticks are bad this year and there’s a disease going around now that’s bobcat fever. It’s when a tick has bitten a bobcat, and it comes and gets on your cats, and it’s pretty much deadly unless you catch it like pretty fast,” Trevathan said.

Bobcat fever is caused by a parasite that the Lone Star tick carries.

Once the tick passes the parasite to a house cat, signs can show up within two weeks.

Without treatment, a cat can die in just two to three days.

Trevathan said the disease is already hitting families in the area.

“Myself and one of the board members, one of our friends lost their cat from it. And she had talked to the vet when they took her out there, and they’d been like seven that week, or in the last two weeks, that they had lost their life from this tick fever,” Trevathan said.

The Lone Star tick is not just a threat to pets; it is also tied to a growing health issue in people.

The tick carries a sugar molecule in its saliva that can trigger alpha-gal syndrome in humans — an allergy to red meat and pork.

Trevathan said cat owners should watch for specific symptoms.

“Watch for lack of energy, getting lethargic. Look at their gums to see if they’re not acting right. Go ahead and take them to the vet and get them checked just to make sure,” Trevathan said.

Trevathan said prevention is the best defense, and it does not have to be complicated.

“It pretty much is just using flea and tick prevention on them, which you can get at a vet, you can get it at Tractor Supply, you can get it at Walmart. As long as you’re putting something on them,” Trevathan said.

Trevathan said she found a tick crawling on her leg on Sunday, and the reminder goes for people, too.

“Just check yourself, check your animals if they’re outside, because you don’t want them to be sick,” Trevathan said.

Experts say tick season usually lasts through the fall, but using prevention year-round is the safest move for pets and people.

payload.title: Kissoihin ja ihmisiin tarttuva sienitauti leviää Etelä-Amerikassa
payload.summary: Sporothrix brasiliensis -sienen aiheuttama tauti on sairastuttanut Etelä-Amerikassa tuhansia kissoja ja yli 11 000 ihmistä sen jälkeen, kun se nousi esiin Brasiliassa 1990-luvulla.
payload.content:
Sporothrix brasiliensis -sienen aiheuttama tauti on levinnyt Etelä-Amerikassa kissojen ja ihmisten terveysuhaksi. Science Newsin mukaan tauti on sairastuttanut ja tappanut tuhansia kissoja sekä tartuttanut yli 11 000 ihmistä ja ainakin 200 koiraa sen jälkeen, kun se havaittiin Brasiliassa 1990-luvulla.

## Tauti näkyy etenkin kissoissa

Sporothrix brasiliensis kuuluu sieniin, jotka voivat aiheuttaa ihon ja kudosten infektioita. Science Newsin kuvaaman asiant…yksen mukaan tauti voi aiheuttaa kissoille vuotavia ihohaavaumia ja muita vakavia oireita. Keskeistä on myös se, että tauti voi siirtyä kissoista ihmisiin.

Kyse ei siis ole vain eläinlääketieteellisestä ongelmasta. Kun tartunta kiertää kissoissa, se voi samalla lisätä ihmisten altistumista. Lähdetietojen perusteella tauti on jo aiheuttanut Etelä-Amerikassa laajan sairastumisten joukon sekä eläimissä että ihmisissä.

## Yhdysvalloissa tautia ei ole virallisesti todettu

Science Newsin mukaan tautia ei tiettävästi ole vielä todettu Yhdysvalloissa viranomaisten tiedossa olevien tapausten perusteella. Jutussa siteerattu CDC:n asiantuntija arvioi kuitenkin, että Sporothrix brasiliensis -sienen saapuminen Yhdysvaltoihin on ajan kysymys.

Arvio kertoo huolesta, mutta lähdetiedot eivät osoita, että tauti olisi jo levinnyt Yhdysvaltoihin. Tämän vuoksi johtopäätös on rajattava siihen, että asiantuntijat seuraavat uhkaa ja pitävät leviämistä mahdollisena.

## Kasvava huomio uusiin sienitauteihin

Tapaus nousi esiin Washingtonissa järjestetyssä ASM Microbe -kokouksessa, jossa käsiteltiin uusia ja esiin nousevia sienitartuntoja. Science Newsin mukaan esityksessä kuvattu tauti herätti huomiota juuri siksi, että se yhdistää vakavat eläinoireet, ihmistartunnat ja laajan leviämisen Etelä-Amerikassa.

Saatavilla oleva lähdeaineisto ei kerro tarkemmin tartuntareiteistä, hoitotuloksista tai siitä, missä Etelä-Amerikan maissa tapauksia on todettu Brasilian ulkopuolella. Varmasti voidaan sanoa, että Sporothrix brasiliensis on noussut merkittäväksi seurattavaksi sienitaudiksi, koska se on jo aiheuttanut huomattavan määrän tartuntoja ihmisissä ja eläimissä.
summary_bullets: Sporothrix brasiliensis -sieni voi tartuttaa kissoja ja ihmisiä.
Tauti on sairastuttanut Etelä-Amerikassa yli 11 000 ihmistä ja tuhansia kissoja.
Yhdysvalloissa tautia ei lähdetietojen mukaan ole virallisesti todettu, mutta asiantuntija pitää leviämistä mahdollisena.
payload.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu rajattuun Science News -lähdeaineistoon. Yksityiskohtia tartuntareiteistä, hoidosta ja maantieteellisestä leviämisestä Brasilian ulkopuolella ei lisätty, koska niitä ei ollut paketissa.
